# Introduction

Ecological information is scattered throughout literature. The
difficulty is that many statistical applications often focus on
obtaining exact solutions to well defined problems (M-closed worlds).
Exact solutions are preferable where they are possible and where they
matter, particularly for causal inference. However, causal inference is
only justified when the premises underlying the causal argument are also
satisfied. It is therefore not the model itself that makes an argument
causal.

In ecology, these premises are frequently constrained by data quality,
study design, and “context dependency” (everything is context
dependent). Differences among species, ecosystems, spatial scales,
experimental conditions (gradient length understood as positivity in
causal inference), and measurement procedures can limit how far
individual models and their associated claims can be generalized. At the
same time, these limitations do not necessarily make the available
information uninformative (M-open worlds).

**HeMiE - Heterodox (Bayesian) Methods in Ecology** focuses on pragmatic
approaches for gathering, re-using, synthesizing, predicting from, and
generalizing ecological information. Rather than requiring all available
information to conform to a single statistical framework, the package
provides methods for combining and evaluating heterogeneous sources of
information. One central development is the **Generalized Bayesian
Meta-analytic Network (GBMN)** framework, which integrates information
from multiple studies and statistical models into predictive networks.

An interactive implementation of the GBMN framework is available through
the [GBMN web application](https://snwikaij.shinyapps.io/ppmn).

HeMiE provides tools for ecological modelling, information synthesis,
prediction, and visualization, with a strong emphasis on Bayesian and
predictive methods. A basic understanding of R is sufficient to use the
core functions, although some familiarity with statistical models,
functions, and variables is useful for applying the methods more
broadly. HeMiE itself is under active development, and its methods,
documentation, and implementation may change as the package develops.

## Installation

The development version of **HeMiE** can be installed directly from
GitHub using `devtools`:

``` r
# Install devtools if necessary
install.packages("devtools")

# Install HeMiE
devtools::install_github("snwikaij/HeMiE")

# Load HeMiE
library(HeMiE)
```

Questions, problems and suggestions for improvements are welcome.

# Package index

## Generalized Bayesian Meta-analytic Networks

Functions for constructing, updating, predicting from, and evaluating
Generalized Bayesian Meta-analytic Networks.

- [`build_gbmn()`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/build_gbmn.md)
  : Build the foundational Generalized Bayesian Meta-analytic Network
  (GBMN)
- [`update_gbmn()`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/update_gbmn.md)
  : Update GBMN function
- [`predict_gbmn()`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/predict_gbmn.md)
  : Predict function for a GBMN object
- [`marginal_gbmn()`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/marginal_gbmn.md)
  : Plots the marginal expectations of each edge function with
  credibility intervals
- [`pred_fit_gbmn()`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/pred_fit_gbmn.md)
  : Predictive fit function to assess performance
- [`disp_gbmn()`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/disp_gbmn.md)
  : Displacement test for GBMN
- [`extract_covar_gbmn()`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/extract_covar_gbmn.md)
  : GBMN correlation matrix extraction
- [`extract_param_gbmn()`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/extract_param_gbmn.md)
  : Extract parameters from object

## Example data

Example datasets for constructing, updating, and evaluating GBMNs.

- [`example1`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/example1.md) :
  Example meta-analytic data for a single GBMN edge
- [`example2`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/example2.md) :
  Example meta-analytic data for a multi-edge GBMN
- [`meta_data`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/meta_data.md)
  : Example meta-analytic data for a larger GBMN
- [`train_data`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/train_data.md)
  : Example training data for updating a GBMN
- [`val_data`](https://snwikaij.github.io/HeMiE/reference/val_data.md) :
  Example validation data for a GBMN
